tldr: GLIDER is an offline hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that introduces a parameter-efficient two-level hierarchy to LLM policies, decomposing long-horizon decision-making tasks into chain-of-thought sub-tasks for improved exploration and credit assignment.
contributions: An offline hierarchical framework GLIDER that empowers LLM agents to tackle complex decision-making tasks via sophisticated exploration and structured reasoning
Fast offline-to-online adaptation to non-stationary environments through training highly generalizable low-level skills
Comprehensive studies on ScienceWorld and ALFWorld benchmarks showing consistent performance gains and generalization improvements over baselines
methods: GLIDER uses a two-layer hierarchical architecture with a high-level policy that plans abstract sub-task goals every c steps and a low-level controller that executes atomic actions. Both policies share a frozen LLM backbone with LoRA adapters for the actor and MLP layers for the critic, achieving parameter efficiency. The pipeline has three stages: (1) base agent construction via supervised fine-tuning (behavior cloning) with length regularization on demonstration trajectories, (2) offline RL refinement using hierarchical actor-critic models where the critic evaluates at the sentence level with implicit Q-learning loss and the actor optimizes via advantage-weighted maximum likelihood at the token level, and (3) offline-to-online adaptation where the low-level skills are frozen and only the high-level policy is fine-tuned on new environments using intrinsic sub-task completion rewards.
results: Experiments on ScienceWorld (30 tasks) and ALFWorld (6 types of household manipulation tasks) benchmarks show GLIDER achieves consistent performance gains and enhanced generalization capabilities, surpassing a range of baselines by a significant margin. The method demonstrates strong sample efficiency through offline training and effective offline-to-online adaptation to non-stationary environments.
